utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to you, Mr. Feldi. Mr. Feldi, I would like to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Carrier. Mr. Carrier is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Carrier, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, with regard to your report, I take it that you understand the importance of being as transparent as possible, in terms of a number of things, and I'll list them for you. Number one, what your instructions were regarding the report; number two, what information and resources you relied upon; number three, what your methodology was that you used to arrive at your opinion. You understand that; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Mr. Carrier, as regards the first part of your question, I received instructions to draft my expert report --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there because --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the focus --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Feldi, I'm going to stop you there. I'm wanting to confirm that you understood the importance of those things. I didn't ask you what they were. Mr. Feldi, you were a member of the Croatian Main Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And do you remember these HV officers as members of the Main Staff as well: Number one, Rajko Rakic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. [In English] Excuse me. [Interpretation] Now I'm receiving interpretation. No, Mr. Rajko Rakic was not in the Main Staff when I was there. He was in the command of the Military District of Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Did you ever know Mr. -- or General Rakic to be a member of the Main Staff ever?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: What about Ivan Pokaz?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Ivan Pokaz was assistant to the head of the intelligence administration at the Main Staff. Later on, he was appointed head of the intelligence administration in the Main Staff of the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: What about Dragutin Repinc?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Repinc came to the Main Staff in 1993. He joined my MPRI team. I acted as assistant to the head of training and education. He became a member of my team. For a while, he stayed with the Main Staff. And later on, he worked in the various commands of the Military Districts. Then you returned to the Main Staff as an operations officer and then went abroad for further schooling. Upon his return, he rejoined the Main Staff again. And he is there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And General Drago Lovric?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Drago Lovric arrived in the Main Staff after Operation Storm. Currently, he is in Brussels with our NATO mission there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the next portion of the cross-examination, I would ask that we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been informed that I should have ask asked to have at least those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be the two documents you're talking about will be MFI'd. Mr. Registrar could you already assign numbers to them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 7387 becomes exhibit number P2631, marked for identification; and 65 ter 7405 becomes exhibit number P2632, also marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. They'll keep that status for the time being. Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, I want to return to something you said about the meetings that you were having with General Lovric, among other people. You said that people would drop in. Was that a regular occurrence; and do you recall specifics about who it was that was dropping in on the meetings when you were having these discussions?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I have to be precise. I did not state that people dropped by during the meetings. Perhaps this was not understood well. While we were working in the archives of the Ministry of Defence, people did come back. However, during the meetings called by General Lovric, which were official, nobody came. At least I'm not aware of it. Perhaps this was misunderstood. Only those who were invited attended the meetings, while we worked in the archives, however, people did drop by, but this is a different thing. These were simply people that we were in touch with. I hope I understood the gist of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Were there people invited to your coordination meetings under General Lovric that were not members of the committee formed under General Lovric?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If General Lovric called the meetings of our team, then no one else attended. If he called meetings with the representatives of General Markac's Defence, then such representatives would attend, as well as Markac and other people they wanted to have from the Ministry of the Interior and his attorneys. I did say that at such meetings Mr. Vlado Rendulic occasionally participated as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we please have document number 65 ter 7411 called up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, the document that is going to appear on the screen in front of you is an 8 August 2005 decision by the Croatian minister of defence Roncevic. And, Mr. Feldi, if I can direct your attention to the paragraph marked number I on page 1, under the words "decision as follows," I'm going to read you this portion. I will be asking you some questions in a moment. "A Working Group will be established consisting of active military persons in the Ministry of Defence and the Main Staff of the Republic of Croatia with the purpose to assist the Defence team of the retired Colonel General Mladen Markac with the analysis and explanation of documentation created in the Ministry of Defence and the Main Staff of the Republic of Croatia armed forces, relating to the [sic] planning and carrying out of the military and police Operation Storm."

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, can you just turn the page in English, and under number II --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Do you see there, Mr. Feldi, it indicates that: "Permanent members of the Working Group were appointed by Roncevic including, Lovric, Repinc, and Skuliber? And the second paragraph of that item number II indicates as follows: "As necessary, at the proposal of the leader of the Work Group, minister of defence will by his decision assign also other persons from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia and of the OSRH or retired officers expert in particular area to join the Working Group, on the basis of work contract for carrying out tasks specified in point I of this decision?" Mr. Feldi, given that you were retired, were you appointed under a work contract by the Ministry of Defence when you performed your work?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. But pursuant to another decision, not this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Feldi, do you have a copy of that decision or a copy of the work contract into which you entered, when you performed your tasks, pursuant to the minister of defence's decision?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, but not with me, however. It is back home. Based on that defence minister's decision which came in the late 2005, I was called to the Main Staff, as I have already explained, and began working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, in your report and in your CV there is no indication about those two documents; the decision or the work contract. Would you be amenable to providing those two documents to the Court?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no reason for me not to. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber appreciates your cooperative attitude, Mr. Feldi, in this respect. What's the best way to then receive the -- Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps can he can help with the logistics if those supporting me are able to do that. If not, perhaps we can come back to the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, or seek the assistance of the Victims and Witness Section because of, of course, I do not know -- I take it that this will materialise after the witness has concluded his testimony. That's -- and then, of course, there is no problem in your offer, Mr. Kay, whereas, if it would be still today or tomorrow then, of course, the Victims and Witness Section would be the appropriate authority to deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I'll see if we can deal with it more quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, I want to go through this decision of Defence Minister Roncevic in order to determine whether or not you were provided with the same resources, access, et cetera, that was provided for under this decision. And if I could ask to you turn your attention to the first part of number III, item number III, which is on page 2 of both the English and the B/C/S. That section indicates: "Working Group from point I of this decision will start working on [sic] 1 September 2005 in the premises of the Central Military Archives, as needed and requested by defence, and it will be active until the completion of the proceedings against the retired Colonel General Mladen Markac conducted before the ICTY." Mr. Feldi, you've already mentioned that you were provided premises in the archives when you conducted your work under General Lovric. Can you tell us whether or not, given that it says that the team will be active until the completion of the proceedings, whether or not you're still a member of -- in any way or associated with the team set up by General Lovric?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I don't know what team was formed by General Lovric. I received the defence minister's decision appointing me a team member of the committee charged with producing an analysis of Operation Storm. However, I see this decision for the first time. There is no mention of the production of any sort of analysis on Operation Storm. In item I, the Working Group is being set up in order to assist Defence of the accused General Markac in the analysis and interpretation of documents but not in the production of any materials. In item III it says that the Working Group - that is to say, Generals, Lovric, Repinc, and Skuliber will work on this until the proceedings conducted before the ICTY against the retired General Mladen Markac are concluded. I don't know of this decision. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: To clarify, Mr. Feldi, in terms of what I'm talking about in terms of a committee under General Lovric. It's the one that we have been talking about all day today, the one that you said you were a member of under General Lovric. And I'm wondering whether or not you are still in any way associated with that committee.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We completed the book, signed it, and handed it over to the Chief of the Main Staff. At that point, all the obligations we had concerning the analysis of Operation Storm ceased. I was not involved in any subsequent work, meetings, or discussions related to the Defence of General Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And can you put a date on that for us? When exactly did your involvement end?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the book bears the date of July 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, when did your involvement end? If you can put a date on that.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could please turn to page 3 in the English, at the top of the page, and remaining in page 2 in the B/C/S, second paragraph of item number III --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, which is top of the page in English reads: "The head and deputy head of the Working Group, at the request of defence and pursuant to a special order of the Ministry of Defence, may appear before the ICTY to serve in the role of expert witness." Mr. Feldi, my question to you is: Did you need any individual person or institution's prior approval before you were allowed to testify before the Tribunal in this case as an expert?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody's approval or order was warranted. I am a retired general of the Croatian Army and a free citizen of the Republic of Croatia. General Lovric and General Repinc are active Generals on the Main Staff. They had to provide an approval from the minister of defence. I, on the other hand, did not require anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, I didn't ask if it was warranted. I just wanted to be clear that you didn't actually have to get anyone's approval. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, if you refer to a document that includes the head and deputy head of a Working Group who are different people as we have seen from the document, it's quite reasonable for the witness to give an explanation as to the difference between their positions and his positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think that that was the issue raised by Mr. Carrier. I think the witness explained that there was no need to seek the approval in view of his position which was different from the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he answered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he has answered that. But even if I do not need anything, I, nevertheless, sometimes -- let's try to clarify this. And the question was not very clear either. Did you discuss with anyone within the circles of the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of the Interior, or whatever ministry, whether it was appropriate for you to serve as an expert witness for the Cermak Defence? Or did you just, without consulting any person related to government circles, did you just accept the invitation by the Cermak Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as was seen yesterday, as early as 2003, I gave a statement to the Prosecution. Likewise, I received a phone call from the Prosecution; they called me home and asked me to give a statement. The call that was placed to me concerning my statement did not go through the government or any other state institution, including the Ministry of Defence. Rather, they phoned me at my home and asked me if I wanted to give a statement in relation to Operation Medak Pocket. And I did. I told the lady minister of defence at the time that I was called. I informed her of it, and she said, Very well, you are a free citizen and you are free to go. They should have approached you through the government office for cooperation, but since they did not, let them know that they should let the office know that you're going. When I was asked by the Defence for General Cermak to get involved in the preparation and drafting of the expert report, there was no need for me to seek and obtain any sort of approval from anyone. I hope my answer has been clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you did not at that time as you did previously communicate with the Ministry of Defence when invited. You just responded to the invitation. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correctly understood, yes. The fact that I'm here today and that I was writing an expert report, this is something that I informed the Chief of the Main Staff of. I did not seek for any official approval, but he is aware of the fact that I wrote the expert report, and he is aware of the fact that I am here. I am a retired general of the HV, and he is, after all, the Chief of the Main Staff of the HV and ought to know what his generals are doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You informed him when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Last spring, when I received the first request for my services. Sometime in February or March earlier this year when Mr. Kay asked me to produce an expert report. I told him that I agreed to producing the report and he said, Very well and you have my support, if you need assistance in anything, let me know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there was communication but not with the purpose of seeking any way of permission or approval. Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, if I could direct your attention to item number IV in this decision which talks about the task of the Working Group. And it says, it terms of a task: "To initiate and coordinate all necessary activities for providing explanation and analyses of documentation created in the Ministry of Defence and the Main Staff of the Republic of Croatia armed forces concerning planning and conducting military and police Operation Oluja; this also implies creation of relevant documents, and performing other tasks according requests of defence." Mr. Feldi, other than the report itself, can you explain whether or not you were ever tasked with creating any documents?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I stated in my CV that, as of 1991, I had been an operations officer in the Croatian Army. The first task to draft a plan of the defence action for the liberation of the Republic of Croatia was received by me in December 1991 from the Chief of the Main Staff Tus. I authored all the subsequent plans --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I'm cutting you off because I just want to know if you were tasked under the committee that you were on, under General Lovric, with creating any documents, other than -- I'm not talking about the report, but if you were tasked with creating any documents in relation to that committee.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, it's no. I myself did not produce a new document, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Feldi. If I could direct your attention now to the next paragraph of item number IV which reads: "Work activities of this Group will be coordinated by the director of Military Security Agency, and every document, in the form of opinion, analysis, elaborate, expertise, and similar, will be previously approved, prior to being submitted to the Defence of General Markac, by the head of the Main Staff ..." Mr. Feldi, my question to you is: During the time you were putting together your report for General Cermak, did you have any specific dealings with the Croatian military security intelligence service relating to your report?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: You've mentioned discussing your -- at least the idea of putting together a report with the Chief of the Main Staff. Did you send a copy of your report to him before you gave it to the Cermak Defence?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I did not speak with the Chief of the Main Staff about my idea of producing a report. I merely informed him that I was working on one such document. I didn't give him a draft or anything, in terms of a copy of my report. I only verbally informed him of the fact that I was working on my report and that I would appear before the Honourable Chamber to present my report. He received this information in February, earlier this year, and the last time I talked to him about it was on the occasion of the festivities in Knin. And if I may add, the only individual who received a copy of my expert report was Mr. Kay. That includes the first draft that I produced thereof and the final version. I provided him with my first draft on which he -- to which he addressed his comments and which I took into consideration when producing the final version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, looking at item number V of this decision, at the bottom it discusses a transfer of documents from the Main Staff to the Central Military Archives during August 2005. Do you have any knowledge about that transfer of documents or what that consisted of?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am one of the authors of all these documents that were in possession of the operations administration of the Main Staff. It was located where the war plan is kept, under strict security. In my administration, there was a separate department for the development of all the analyses of the Croatian Army, and that documentation is stored in the administration. Now I see that pursuant -- I see pursuant to this decision's -- decision -- minister's decision that he ordered that all these documents be transferred from the Main Staff from where the war plans were stored to the Central Military Archives of the -- of the Ministry of Defence. You will know that when I left the Main Staff, the documentation was still there. Now, about the -- the information that it was transferred in August 2005 is something that I am seeing here for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, just with regard to number 6 of this order which discusses the expenses in regard to the activity for this committee are to be borne by, first off, the officer -- or the office of the minister of defence and thereafter the Main Staff. When you were conducting your analysis under General Lovric, is that how it worked as well, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every month General Lovric signed a receipt to the effect that I and other members of the team worked on the material needed for the production of the book analysis of Operation Storm and sent it to the personnel Department of the MOD which, in turn -- on his request asked from the accountancy service to pay remuneration for our work. The expenses incurred were roughly 500 euros a month, and the remuneration for the expenses incurred was something that was credited to my account. In December 2006, my contract was no longer valid, and in 2007 I no longer received any sort of remuneration for the simple fact that I did no further work, as the book was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could have that document admitted in into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number P2633.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2633 is admitted into evidence. I have to add to this, that the previously admitted -- the MFI documents, P2631 and P2632, should be under seal. They're still MFI'd. Mr. Carrier, we're close to a point where we would have a break. Would this be a suitable moment, Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: If I could ask one more question it would close off this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I remember that you earlier said that you asked one question which took approximately 20 minutes, but I'm exaggerating. One question I consider to be finished within two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I think the question will be shorter, at least, than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, you didn't mention this in your report or your CV but isn't it the case that, back in 1992, you were appointed to a commission by President Tudjman, and on that commission - which was only five people - you served actually under General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, can you please remind me what sort of commission this was? I was on a great many commissions. I'm not sure which one you're referring to, back in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the one that was headed by General Cermak that consisted of five people that you were appointed to?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1992 when I was Major-General, unless I'm mistaken. And it was a commission headed by General Cermak. Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a good place to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would first likes to Madam Usher to escort the witness. We'll have a break, Mr. Feldi. We'd like to see you back in approximately 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, looking at Rule 90(H), the Chamber wonders what we're dealing with at this moment. Apparently your cross-examination is not focussing on the subject matter of the evidence in-chief. We also did not gain the impression that this witness is giving evidence which is relevant for the Prosecution's case, at least subject matter of the Prosecution case. What then remains is credibility issues. Is our understanding correct, that we are dealing in two full sessions now with credibility issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: We're dealing with credibility issues and, pursuant to the Chamber's decision, about exploring transparency. That is finished now anyway, Mr. President. I intend now to move to the next part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because that could have been done in approximately 25 percent of the time you used for that. Get to the core of the issue more quickly, and do not explore all the details. Of course it's fine for us to know now that finally the expenses that receipts were handed out, et cetera, you are in control of your cross-examination, and it should be done more efficiently. We'll have a break, and we resume at --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- to assist the Court. I'm told by my team that they may be able to assist General Feldi in the collection of this contract, if their service is needed. If Victims and Witnesses Unit are needed to do it, they can do it. I don't mind subcontracting it. But if anyone wants assistance, we have contacted people in Zagreb who would be able to go to a place for him to collect it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would please briefly discuss it with Mr. Carrier whether he with would have any problem in such an involvement at this moment of the Cermak Defence in obtaining those documents. Mr. Carrier, if you would discuss it. If any problem then remains, then, of course, I take it that you will address the Chamber again on the matter, or that you seek ways of getting the Victims and Witness Section involved. It seems to be a rather -- well, to say kind of a neutral matter, contracts, documents. Mr. Carrier, you're willing to discuss it with Mr. Kay over the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then we'll hear the results. We will resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, you draw a number of conclusions about the military police. That's contained in part 1.5.50 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Page reference is 38 and 39, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Feldi, if I can ask you to specifically turn your attention to the paragraphs 1.5.10 through to 13 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Which is on pages 23 to 24 of the B/C/S; that's page 26, 27, of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And I want to turn your attention to the specific parts where you discuss the temporary instructions for the work of the units of the military police of the Croatian Army dated 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Document reference, Your Honours, is D993.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Feldi, before we start, I just want to clarify something. Is it your position that, as a result of passing the temporary instructions, that the military police units, under that instruction, were subordinated solely to the military police in terms of their regular tasks in the field. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You find it in item 1.5.10, if I understood you well, in which it is stated correctly that MP units are subordinated to the military police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please call up Exhibit D993 and turn to page 4 in the English and same page, 4, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, as this comes up, I want to go through a couple of sections with you and draw your attention to them and then ask you a few questions about them. Looking at the temporary instructions at page 4, paragraph 2, it says that these instructions cover: fundamentals of military police organisation; fundamentals of command and control; and the scope of activities of the military police in peace and war. And directly under that it indicates that: "The instructions are aimed for: members of the military police for consistent handling of tasks within its scope of activity; officers of commands, units, and institutions of the Croatian Army of which the military police are part for consistent command and control and the use of these units."

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 5 in the English and 5 in the B/C/S. And if we can focus, please, on item number VI.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, this is a -- this is a point from the temporary instructions that you didn't specifically -- or explicitly deal with in your report and it reads: "The MP units or their commanders carry out all military police tasks on request by the commander of the Republic of Croatia armed forces unit where they are engaged." And then in brackets it lists a number of different pieces, battalion, brigade, et cetera, operations group. Now, Mr. Feldi, what I'm trying to understand is in your report, in your analysis, you didn't make any explicit reference or you just seemed to analyse these particular sections of the temporary instructions which I'm going suggest to you indicate that in fact MP units are to carry out military police tasks on the orders of the HV commander where they are engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could we have a date as to when the analysis by counsel iis being sought?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have the same objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I took it that it would be when the temporary instructions were in force, but perhaps you specify that, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Certainly. I was talking about the proposition which I put to Mr. Feldi in the beginning, that he says that the temporary instructions solely subordinated the units to the military police administration, so I'm trying to figure out his analysis with regard to that, because having looked at the report, it -- -- it develops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question, at this moment, is limited to the time when these temporary rules applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Feldi, given the parts that we just looked at in these temporary rules, can you explain how it is that you conclude that, under the temporary instructions, the military police units are only subordinated to the military police administration?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, in item 1 on the same page it says that within the Ministry of Defence there should be a military police administration, which commands and controls all military police units, irrespective of their location. Pursuant to that, I concluded that it is only the military police administration that has the right to order all military police units, as regulated by the provisional instructions of the 6th of January, 1992. In item 6 that you read out, one finds that the military police units and their commanders carry out all military police tasks on request by the commander of the armed forces unit. In this item, no right is given to the commanders of army units to command military police units. It is clearly stated in item 1 that only the military police administration enjoys that right. If they put through a request, then the police administration can issue an order on engagement of the various MP units. In my view, the comment made in item 6 was an unnecessary one, since item 1 is clear in and of itself. It is unambiguous.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: You indicate that item 1 says that only the military police administration has that right. How do you -- where are you reading in the word "only"? How do you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, within the Ministry of Defence, there is no other administration and the Chief of the Main Staff was not assigned the right to command the military police by virtue of these instructions. The military police is subordinated only to the chief of the military police administration. If I may, Mr. Carrier, in my report, I have referred to these instructions as a result of the dissatisfaction of the military police administration with the state of things in MP units --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, I'm going to cut you off; I have limited time. I'm not asking you about that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think that may have been a very relevant piece of evidence to come out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would like the witness to finish his answer. Could you please -- you were about to explain that this temporary rules were the result of dissatisfaction. Could you please finish that part of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The temporary instructions, as I have mentioned in my expert report, came about after an amount of work undertaken by the military police administration trying to regain their right to command military police units. I documented that in my report in several items, the first of which is the decision of the president on the structure of the Ministry of Defence, introducing the MP administration. Not to be command and control but to be at the service of all military police units within the Croatian Army. During December 1991, the chief of the military police administration, General Lausic, according to his statement, which he gave here, he visited the operational zone in Osijek. He was dissatisfied with the military police carrying out orders of the military operational zone commander and not his orders, and that is why, upon his return, he proposed these new rules to the minister of defence. In the new rules, under item 1, the minister orders that the MP administration command and control all MP units, irrespective of their location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You explained what the dissatisfaction was which led to the adoption of these rules, but we have dealt with the first article already and what it contains. Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar could we please have Exhibit P1206, please, and turn to page 3 in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, while this document is coming up, if you can look at paragraphs 1.5.14 to 1.5.16 of your report; that's page 27 to 28 in the English and 24, 25, in the B/C/S. Mr. Feldi, in this part of your report you discuss an order that had been issued by General Lausic after a meeting of the Military Defence Council -- or, sorry, Military Council in December 1992 where command and control of military police units of was one of the items on the agenda. Now at paragraph 1.5.16, you indicate that you analysed that at the conclusions of that session of the Military Council of the Ministry of Defence, other than listing General Lausic's order dated 17 December 1992, there's no other material referenced, so it's not clear what exactly you relied on when you said that you analysed it. Is it just General Lausic's order, or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I personally attended the Military Council meeting. I know that there was some serious discussion about who orders -- commands the military police. In the preamble of the order that you refer to, which is P01206 of the 17th of December, 1992, there is an explanation as to why he issued that order. At that meeting of the Military Council, it was requested that there should be a clear system of subordination within the military police, in terms of vertical subordination, as well as horizontal coordination, between the various, same-level units within the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, are you finished?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This, in turn, required that the chief of the MP administration follows through the conclusions of the Military Council and puts into practice the temporary instructions assigning him that authority. In keeping with the conclusions of the Military Council --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The chief of the MP administration or the administration itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If could you keep an eye on the translation it was the French translation that needed some additional time. Mr. Feldi, I would also -- if we make a pause it's usually to enable interpreters and transcribers to do their job. If you start during such a break to -- completing your answer, of course, if there's any important thing to add, please to do so, but, otherwise, wait until Mr. Carrier has put his next question to you. Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, given what you just answered, are you saying that this document from General Lausic in December 1992 was implementing the temporary instructions? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was still discussing the session of the Military Council, which took place in the MOD where I attended. Based on the conclusions of that session of the Military Council, the chief of the military police administration issued his order, which is P01206. You yourself referred to that document when putting the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Okay. So you said you were in attendance at that Military Council. You're aware their General Lausic also attended that Military Council; correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I am aware of that. Excuse me. I know that because I was there, and I know that he, as the chief of the MP administration, submitted a part of his report on the work of the military police during that session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, in terms of the transcript I just wanted to be sure that I put this on the record. Page 72, line 13, I believe there's a word missing from the transcript after the word horizontal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, I'll read to you what we have on the transcript: "At that meeting of the Military Council, it was requested that there should be a clear system of subordination within the military police, in terms of vertical subordination, as well as horizontal ..." And did you then add a word after "horizontal"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did, Your Honour. Horizontal coordination and cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we find it in the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Carrier, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, in your report at paragraph 1.5.16 you indicate that, as a result of this order from General Lausic, that the military police administrations' primary task in relation to the military police was responsibility for the professional military training, combat readiness, and the state of MP units, and, at the same time, Croatian Army commanders were given command and control over MP units in the operative zones. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And are you also aware that that is General Lausic's understanding, in terms of -- not that it changed anything, but that's how the system of military police subordination was supposed to work, at least at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to object to the question as formulated at page 74, lines 20 to 22. I don't find where the witness's reports says Croatian Army commanders were given command and control over MP units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, you said 1.5.16.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And the paragraph below that as well, in combination but specifically 1.1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently there is an problem with the way in which you summarised it. Could you try to summarise it in such a way or to read the relevant portions so as to avoid any misunderstanding or any confusion. We could have a battle for ten minutes how it could be best summarized. Try to do your best.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I'll try, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, is it your position that, under P1206, which is General Lausic's December 1992 order, that the HV army units are, in fact, the ones that command and control MP units in the operative zones?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A clarification, please. Before the order, in my statement, I said that towards the end of 1991 and until the provisional instructions were put in place, the military police was commanded by the various HV commanders at the level of operational zones and brigades. By virtue of the temporary instructions, that right was taken away from the commanders of the operational zones and the various HV units. In item 1, the MP administration of the MOD was the sole body that had the right to command and control MP units. At the session of the Military Council, it was concluded that that needs to be changed and that commanders of the HV need to regain the right to command HV units and that the military police administration become -- should become an MP administration solely as an expert body of the MOD to assist in the developing and implementing policies concerning the military police. Therefore, on the 17th of December, General Lausic issued an order to that effect, stating that the commanders of HV units or commanders of the garrisons within which -- in the -- in whose area of responsibility there are military police units should command those military police units. In the carrying out of all military police tasks, Lausic sent this order to all the commanders of the brigade -- military police brigades, and so on and so forth. I don't know whether this sufficiently clarifies the process which resulted in the order following the Military Council session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Mr. Feldi, if we turn to items number --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: -- 5 and 6 of the General Lausic order from December 1992. If you look at those, I will read them so there's no confusion. But they indicate that there should be coordinating meetings and reporting back to the HV commanders, but let me read it to you. Number 5: "MP unit commanders are obliged to be present at all coordinating meetings called by the HV unit commander to whom they are subordinated in the implementation of their daily tasks." And item number 6: "MP unit commanders shall copy their daily reports to the HV commanders to whom they are subordinated. "Military police battalion commanders shall copy their monthly activity reports to the relevant HV OZ commanders." Now, Mr. Feldi, as an expert and given the -- the subordination of MP units to HV commanders under this order, or at least spelling it out, in terms of these coordinating meetings described and given how you've made mention of reporting, et cetera, in your report, would you agree that MP unit commanders' presence in these coordinating meetings with their superior HV commanders would facilitate the HV commanders's ability to supervise and issue orders to his subordinated MP units, carrying out daily tasks while, at the same time, facilitate military police reporting to the HV commander to whom they're subordinated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Objection. It is not only compound, it's multiply compound. And, secondly, I object to the formulation to "their superior HV commander." I don't think there is anything that has been established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you replace the word "superior HV commanders" by commanders -- "HV commanders" to which they were subordinated, we follow the text exactly of -- of paragraph 5. Could you please answer the question, whether the -- that this presence would facilitate the ability to supervise and issue orders to subordinated military police units. That's the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I answer the first part of the question right now, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Coordination meetings are standard procedure in the work of a command. Coordination meetings constitute preparation for certain tasks and actions. And the commander will invite his subordinated commanders to such coordination meetings, in order to agree on certain matters with him -- with them, coordinate with them, and to prepare orders that he would convey to them. Coordination meetings also attended by commanders of the military police confirm that they were subordinated to the HV commander who organised such meetings. Item 5 is quite clear on that score.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would the presence during such meetings also facilitate the reporting to the HV commanders to which they were subordinated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. One of the reasons why such coordination meetings are held is to report on the tasks carried out previously, as well as the agreement and coordinations on the impending tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Now, Mr. Registrar, if we could please turn to page 2 in English and page 1 in the B/C/S of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And at the top of the document in English, Mr. Feldi, General Lausic says: "To help you fully understand and appreciate the above ..." And just to be clear, this is about the conclusions reached at the Military Council, regarding MP command and control. And it goes on: "... as well as to implement it in practice, please find the following clarification in connection with command and control ..." And just below that, Mr. Feldi, there's a description of the various ways in which the military police administration controls and commands all of the units of the military police, and then it lists a number of items. And my question is: Are any of these items listed in the command and control from the military police administration over units of the military police, are any of those things inconsistent with the simultaneous assignment of large authorities to HV operational zone commanders over the military police?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Well, my question is this: The list of things that the military police administration can command and control, is that in any way inconsistent with HV units having command and control over military police units in the operational zones?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the conclusions --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I need to advise the Court that have I switched into the B/C/S translation and "command and control," as the Court is well aware, is a term of art; and I don't believe that term of art is being translated to the witness as that term of art is used in the Croatian armed forces. And so I'm going to have an objection to the "command and control" question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, do you speak any English, Or do you understand the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you take off your earphones for a second. Mr. Misetic, I'm not following the B/C/S translation as you will understand. What I'd like to do is the following: That you suggest what the translation you consider best expressing "command and control" in B/C/S as a technical or state-of-the-art term, and then I'd like to hear from the B/C/S booth, not knowing how they translated it, whether this would meet any objection from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would be happy to. I will also draw the Court's attention and the attention of the parties to the fact that I believe Mr. Theunens had a long direct examination with Mr. Waespi precisely on this phrase, and where it comes from, et cetera. So we actually have stuff on the record on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I could start rereading it. But I would rather revolve the matter at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe the phrase is "vodjenje i zapovedanje."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will now switch to channel 6 to see whether this meets any concerns from the B/C/S booth. Having received full agreement by the B/C/S booth, Mr. Carrier, I would invite you to, again, put the question to the witness, because it's already a few seconds ago, and then we'll hear the answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, the question was whether the list of things that you see under the items that the military police administration excerpts command and control over the military police units, whether that in any way is inconsistent with HV units, at the same time, having command and control over military police units in the operational zones?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, it is not inconsistent, because it lists the tasks of the military police which are binding on the -- which make it incumbent upon the military police administration to take care of the condition of the forces, the level of training, the equipment they had at their disposal, and so on. It has nothing to do with the commands over the military police units out in the field. The order, in its own right, clearly states that the HV commanders are in command of HV military units in all the military police-related tasks. This is not something that is stated among the tasks of the MP administration, and this -- these powers were not granted to it at the time meeting of the Military Council. As you see, all of this was sent to the deputy minister of defence Markica Rebic and the operations administration that was headed by myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question was whether it was inconsistent. You answered that question and then you continued to tell us to whom it was sent which was not part of the question. Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Now, your position is that this December 1992 order from General Lausic changed the command and control system. You said it was different in -- in 1991 before that time HV units had control. Then it was the military police administration under the temporary instructions. And correct me if I'm wrong but your position is that this December 1992 order changes the system of command and control over military police units in the field and grants that power to the HV unit commanders. That's right, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the witness not already told us this? Even not invited to do so to give -- that was how it was, then the HV commanders were deprived, and then it was restored. I mean, is it not rather repetitious, Mr. Carrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I want to make sure that he is saying that it's this order that did that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if could you simply answer with a yes or no, Mr. Feldi, then we could continue. I heard you say that already a couple of times. Did I understand your testimony well in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, given that the words that General Lausic used that this is a clarification in respect of this 1992 December order, and given that -- unless I'm mistaken, the temporary instructions are not even mentioned in this December 1992 order, can you explain how it is, or why it is not stated what General Lausic is doing is changing the system of command and control, explicitly saying that it's going to be different from now on?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, what you referred to has not been stated explicitly. However, this is what the document states at the very end. The above-mentioned order, or the order hereof, shall be effective forthwith. Is that not explicit enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Feldi, that line just says that this order comes into effect. I'm trying to ask you to explain to us why, if it changed everything, and it changed all the -- or it changed the command and control issued under the temporary instructions. Why are the temporary instructions not mentioned, and why wouldn't have General Lausic have said that explicitly? Not about when it came into effect. But can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the council meeting, no conclusion was adopted that the temporary instructions should be made null and void. The temporary instructions not were the subject of discussions at all. What was discussed was the system that existed within the coordination of the military police. It was concluded that the system was not good enough, and it was down to the chief of the military police administration to change the system. And he copied the conclusions from that meeting to all those who were competent to receive it as well as to the military police that needed to implement them. And they were in force until the rules governing the military police were in fact issued. Up until that point, the order issued by the head of the military police administration remained valid and in force.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, given that you said that the system of command and control over the military police units in the operational zones had changed pursuant to the temporary instructions, now you're saying that when the decision was made at the Military Council to change that system entirely, at least with regard to that item, that the temporary instructions weren't even discussed at all in that meeting? And can you explain why that would be and why there would be no reference in this specific order? That's what we're trying to understand. Because the Prosecution's position is that this order, given that it doesn't reference the temporary instructions, didn't change anything under those instructions.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO FELDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, the document P01206, according to that document, the chief of the military police administration does not state anywhere that this document was on the agenda of the council meeting. No. What was discussed was the existing command system. The rules or temporary instructions or any other specific document were not discussed at this meeting. Rather, what was discussed was the practice experienced out in the field, in order to rectify the situation, conclusions were issued which the chief of the MP administration included in the order that he addressed to all those whom -- whom it concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I'm looking at the clock. First of all, Mr. Feldi, I would like to instruct you, as I did yesterday, that you shouldn't speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given today or yesterday or still to be given tomorrow. Madam Usher, could you escort Mr. Feldi out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00, Mr. Feldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still owe you an answer concerning the document. I should like to know whether you are taking it upon yourself as the Trial Chamber to obtain the analysis of Operation Storm and thus releasing me of the obligation to do that myself, including the documents, the minister's decision to -- assigning me to that job of producing an analysis, and my work contract. Am I still under the obligation to provide that to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would leave that for a minute until tomorrow morning, as far as The Blue Book is concerned, we will hear further submissions by the parties tomorrow. And as far as your appointment and the contract is concerned, the Chamber was informed by the parties that they will be able to resolve that so that you don't have to bother about that. Is that correct, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It will need General Feldi, I'm told, to phone his wife and give her the instruction as to where they can be found. That's what I have been told by those who know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Feldi, I hope you are in command and control when you phone your wife. So what is suggested to you that you give a phone call to your wife, that you do not discuss with her your testimony, but nevertheless tell her where these two documents can be found. If you would be willing to do so, that would be highly appreciated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to make a suggestion that would be a better one or an easier one. Could your technical staff get into contact with the Ministry of Defence and ask them to send you a facsimile of all these documents? That would be an end to the story. That would be the personnel administration of the Ministry of Defence. If you will allow me, I'll get in touch with them and ask them to telefax both of the documents and you'll get them in -- as a facsimile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's use all the possible channels, which means that you are still invited to call your wife, apart from anyone else solely discussing that you would agree with these documents to be provided to whomever fetches them in order to deliver them to the parties and to the Court here. Thank you. Madam Usher, could you escort Mr. Feldi out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, it may not come as a surprise. Your time estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes, it was four sessions, was my original time estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you stick to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber already expresses its concerns at this moment about the balance between examination in chief and cross-examination. We will further look into this matter. Could the other Defence teams, and could you, Mr. Kay, tell us whether you would need time for re-examination and how much time you would need as matters stand now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will review matters this afternoon but if I did re-examine, it would be some 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I hear from the other parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we do anything, it will be less than -- less than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll start the next witness later tomorrow. Yes. We adjourn, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 24th of September, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of September, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
